title: Manifest Validation Report
description: Output of `capability-manifest validate --format json`. Contract between the Mission 4 validator and automation that acts on its results, such as the validation step of the contribution workflow (Mission 5). Exit code 0 means no errors, 1 means validation errors, 2 means a usage or I/O error. A valid manifest is not an approved one, and each result reports the completeness level the manifest reaches. Finding codes are listed in docs/manifest-spec.md; new codes may be added in later report format versions.

supportedSchemaVersions.description: Manifest schema versions the validator supports.

invalid.description: Manifests with at least one error.

notice.description: What structural validity does not establish.

file.description: Path of the manifest file as given to the validator.

id.description: id as declared in the manifest, which may itself be invalid; absent if not declared.

capabilityType.description: capabilityType as declared in the manifest, which may itself be invalid; absent if not declared.

schemaVersion.description: schemaVersion as declared in the manifest, which may be malformed; absent if not declared.

validatedAgainst.description: Schema version actually applied; null when the manifest could not be validated against any schema.

valid.description: True when the manifest has no error findings.

checks.description: Status per check: the worst severity among its findings; skipped when Stage 2 did not run.

completeness.description: Completeness level reached by a structurally valid manifest, with the facts each higher level still needs; null when the manifest failed structural validation.

severity.description: error: violates the contract; warning: valid but likely wrong; unverified: could not be confirmed.

path.description: JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) into the manifest; empty for the whole document.

line.description: Line in the source file, when known.

column.description: Column in the source file, when known.

hint.description: How to fix it, or what to do next.

related.description: Ids of the other manifests involved, for findings about shared sources or publications.

level.description: Highest level reached: a level defined by the manifest schema's x-completenessLevels, or 'none' when not even the first level is reached.

unmet.description: For every level the schema defines, in order, the facts of that level that the manifest does not state; an empty list means the level's own facts are stated.
